# How do I connect to the Pylon MCP Server?

Last updated: October 29, 2026

The Pylon MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com provides AI tools access to your Pylon data. The endpoint uses HTTPS, so the connection is protected with TLS. It uses OAuth authentication with your Pylon account.

The application you connect to Pylon's MCP will only have access to data you would have access to in Pylon, and will read and write on behalf of you.

## Common Clients

### Claude Code
    
    `claude mcp add pylon --transport http https://mcp.usepylon.com/`

Then, in Claude Code, run the `/mcp` command and select the `pylon` MCP to authenticate.

`--transport http` selects MCP's Streamable HTTP transport and stateless request handling; it does not mean that the connection is unencrypted or uses a plaintext HTTP URL. The Pylon endpoint remains HTTPS/TLS-protected.

### Claude Desktop and Web

In "Admin Settings", add a custom connector named "Pylon" with URL `https://mcp.usepylon.com/`

Leave "OAuth Client ID" and "OAuth Client Secret" blank.

Navigate to "Settings > Connectors" and click the "Connect" button next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

### ChatGPT

Image: CleanShot 2026-02-19 at 20.26.36.png

In the Apps tab, search for Pylon and install our native ChatGPT app.

### Cursor

Add to your Cursor MCP settings:

`~/.cursor/mcp.json` :
    
    `{
      "mcpServers": {
        ...
        "pylon": {
          "url": "https://mcp.usepylon.com/"
        }
        ...
      }
    }`

Navigate to "Cursor Settings > Tools & MCP" and click "Connect" next to the Pylon MCP to authenticate.

# Authentication

How to authenticate with Pylon's API

The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:

Copy
    
    `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

Generate an API token in the Pylon dashboard.

Once creating a token, you can hit the `/me` endpoint to retrieve details about your organization to confirm your token is working as expected.

Actions performed by the token will show up with name of the token.

MCP connectors now live on Settings > AI controls > Connectors, alongside Pylon's built-in tools, API tools, and codebase connectors.

## Authentication

Custom MCP connectors in Pylon support two authentication patterns:

  * OAuth - Pylon's MCP client connects over Streamable HTTP and implements the MCP authorization spec (2025-06-18), using PKCE (RFC 7636) and discovering OAuth endpoints via Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) and Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414).

  * Static token methods - the connector form also supports bearer token, `API-Key`, `X-Api-Key`, and Basic authentication for MCP servers that accept those headers.

For OAuth-based MCP connections, a connector can obtain its OAuth client in one of two ways:

  * Dynamic Client Registration - if the MCP server advertises a registration endpoint per RFC 7591, Pylon registers itself automatically on the first connect, so no Client ID is required.

  * Manual Client ID - for servers that don't support dynamic registration, register an OAuth app with the provider yourself and paste the Client ID and, optionally, the Client Secret into the connector.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Pylon MCP server?

ImageImage

MCP is an open standard that lets AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor connect to external products. Pylon’s MCP server exposes your Pylon workspace (issues, accounts, contacts, and more) to those tools over OAuth 2.0 or an API token, so your team can query and act on support data from the AI clients they already use.

Which AI tools can connect to Pylon via MCP?

ImageImage

Is the Pylon MCP server secure?

ImageImage

Connections use OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions run as the signed-in user or the token’s identity, with that identity’s current role and permissions. No extra permissions are granted. The identity also needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include.

How do I set up the Pylon MCP server?

ImageImage

Open Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server in Pylon, copy your regional URL (https://mcp.usepylon.com or https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com), and add it in your AI tool (or install the ChatGPT app). Sign in with OAuth, or send an existing API token in an Authorization: Bearer header if your client supports it.

# How do I create a Pylon API token?

Last updated: August 29, 2026

Applies to: Pylon API access

To create a Pylon API token, sign in as a user with permission to manage API tokens, then open Settings → API Tokens. If you do not see that page, ask a workspace admin to create the token or update your access.

  1. Open Settings → API Tokens.

  2. Select Create.

  3. Enter a token name, then finish creation.

  4. Copy the token immediately and store it in a secure location. Pylon only shows the full token value once.

Use the token to authenticate Pylon API requests with a Bearer header:

  * `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

If you need read-only access, a workspace admin should choose an appropriate role for the token when creating it.

This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request: Copy Authorization: Bearer <token> Generate an API token in the Pylon dashboard . API regions Pylon’s API is available in two regions. Use the base URL that matches where your Pylon tenant is hosted: US region: https://api.usepylon.com EU region: https://api.eu.usepylon.com Both regions use the same API endpoints and authentication. Configure your integration to use the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted. You can tell a token's region from its prefix: Prefix Region pylon_api_eu_ EU pylon_api_ US Tokens created before prefixes were introduced have no prefix. Sending a token to the other region's API returns 401 with the wrong_region_token error code, and the message names the correct URL. Once you've created a token, call the /me endpoint to retrieve details about your organization and confirm your token works. Create an API token Only Admins can create and manage API tokens. Go to Settings > Integrations & dev > API . On the Tokens tab, click Create API Token . Enter a Name . Choose who the token acts as: Leave Act as user or bot (optional) empty to give the token its own identity. Pick a Role to control what it can access, and optionally upload an icon. Or select a teammate or bot. The token uses that user's current role and permissions. Optionally, add an IP allowlist (see below). Click Create and copy the token. Pylon shows it only once. Tokens don't expire, and their access is controlled only by the role. There are no separate scopes. Roles A token with its own identity uses the role you pick when you create it. You can change the role later with Edit . Older tokens that have no role act as Admin. A token that acts as a user or bot has no role of its own. It always uses that user's current role, so changing the user's role changes what the token can do. See Roles and user management for what each role allows. Who actions are attributed to Token with its own identity: actions show up under the token's name and icon. Token that acts as a user or bot: actions are attributed to that user or bot. Bots Bots are identities for automation, so API activity is attributed to the bot instead of to a teammate. Bots can't sign in to Pylon. To create one, go to Settings > Workspace > Users , open the Bots tab, and click New Bot . Give it a name, an avatar, and a role. Then select the bot under Act as user or bot when you create a token. IP allowlist Add IP addresses (for example 203.0.113.10 ) or CIDR blocks (for example 203.0.113.0/24 ) to restrict where the token can be used. You can add up to 20 entries. If the list is empty, the token works from any IP. Pylon checks the public IP address your requests come from, so add the public egress IPs or ranges of the servers that call the API. Private addresses such as 10.0.0.0/8 or 192.168.0.0/16 never match. A request from an address that isn't on the list returns 401 with the invalid_api_token error code. Manage tokens The Tokens tab shows each token's Acts as , Token preview , Role , Created by , Last used , and Created values. From the … menu on a token you can: Edit: change the name, role, or IP allowlist. Duplicate Token: create a new token with the same settings. Rotate: generate a new token value. The current token stops working immediately. Delete: permanently revoke the token. Calls using it stop working immediately. View Activity: open the token's request logs. Review API request logs Only Admins can view request logs. Go to Settings > Integrations & dev > API and open the Logs tab, or choose View Activity from a token's … menu to see only that token's requests. Filter by token, or choose All tokens , and by a date range of up to 90 days. The range defaults to the last 7 days. Each request shows when it was made, the token, who it acted as, the method, endpoint, response status, source IP, user agent, and request ID. Requests made with a token that was since deleted still appear. Requests rejected for authentication or rate limits aren't logged, and older requests may not show a token. When tokens are revoked automatically When a user is deactivated, Pylon deletes: every API token that user created, and every API token that acts as that user. Before you deactivate someone who created tokens your integrations rely on, create replacement tokens from another Admin's account. An Admin who has created Admin-role tokens can't be moved to a different role until those tokens are deleted. Previous API Next API conventions Last updated 26 days ago Was this helpful? pages.text: How do I connect a custom MCP to Pylon? | Pylon Knowledge Base Docs Changelog Go to Pylon Docs Changelog Go to Pylon How do I connect a custom MCP to Pylon? Last updated 20 days ago If a system you use exposes an MCP server, an admin can add it to Pylon as a custom MCP connector. Its tools then become available to Pylon's AI agents, including the Assist agent in Pylon and in Slack, Support agents, and Automations, within the permissions you set. Note: Only admins can add custom MCP connectors. Once a connector is added, teammates connect their own accounts from the same Connectors page. See How to connect a custom MCP connector? Add a custom MCP connector Go to Settings > AI controls > Connectors . Click Add Connector > Custom MCP connector . Enter a Name and a useful Description . Teammates see these on the Connectors page, and agents use the description to decide when the connector is relevant. Enter the MCP server URL from the service's MCP documentation or your internal MCP details. Select the authentication method the server supports: OAuth , Bearer token , API-Key , X-API-Key , or Basic auth , and complete the fields shown. Add Custom headers only if the server requires non-authentication metadata. Click Save , then complete any authorization steps the server asks for. Configure connections and tool access After you save the connector, open it and go to Org settings : Connection types - turn on Personal (each teammate uses their own account), Shared (one org account that teammates fall back to), and Agent (a service account for Support agents and Automations) as needed. Connect the Shared and Agent accounts here. Tool access - set each read-only and write/delete tool to Everyone , Some , or No one . Teammates can then choose Always allow , Needs approval , or Blocked for the tools they have access to. For details on each setting, see Connectors & Tool Permissions . Authentication Custom MCP connectors in Pylon support two authentication patterns: OAuth - Pylon's MCP client connects over Streamable HTTP and implements the MCP authorization spec (2025-06-18) , using PKCE (RFC 7636) and discovering OAuth endpoints via Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) and Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414) . Static token methods - the connector form also supports bearer token, API-Key , X-Api-Key , and Basic authentication for MCP servers that accept those headers. For OAuth-based MCP connections, a connector can obtain its OAuth client in one of two ways: Dynamic Client Registration - if the MCP server advertises a registration endpoint per RFC 7591 , Pylon registers itself automatically on the first connect, so no Client ID is required. Manual Client ID - for servers that don't support dynamic registration, register an OAuth app with the provider yourself and paste the Client ID and, optionally, the Client Secret into the connector. If the connection doesn't work with the Client Secret, try removing it in both places: the OAuth app registration page and the Pylon connector settings. Tokens are stored encrypted and refreshed automatically. Can I connect a public MCP server with no authentication? No. Pylon requires either an OAuth-capable MCP server or a supported static credential. A public MCP server with no authentication and no credential to store cannot be connected. What to do instead If your goal is to make public documentation searchable in Pylon AI features, add the public site as Training Data instead. If the system does not expose an MCP server you can use, add a Custom API tool from Add Connector for supported API-based workflows. Frequently Asked Questions Where did the MCP section of the Integrations page go? MCP connectors now live on Settings > AI controls > Connectors , alongside Pylon's built-in tools, API tools, and codebase connectors. Do teammates need to connect their own accounts? Only if you turn on the Personal connection type and want each teammate's actions to use their own identity. If you set up a Shared connection, teammates who haven't connected use it instead. Can I limit which tools from the MCP server are available? Yes. Under Org settings > Tool access , set any tool or group to Some or No one . Trusted by 1,800+ B2B customers globally What is Pylon’s MCP server? Deploy AI agents that handle questions end-to-end, gather context for your team, and escalate to humans when it matters. Can ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor use Pylon data? Yes. Point a supported MCP client at your regional Pylon MCP URL, sign in with OAuth or use an API token, and work issues, accounts, contacts, and your knowledge base from the AI tool you already use. For ChatGPT, you can also install Pylon’s native ChatGPT app from Settings > Plugins (some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins). See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP. Is access scoped to each user? Yes. Every action runs as the authenticated user. The server cannot return data that user cannot see in Pylon, or write changes that user cannot already make in the UI. Connecting needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Can engineers investigate from their editor? Yes. Tools like Claude Code or Cursor can open a Pylon issue, pull message history, and keep working in the same flow your team already uses for debugging. Opening a pull request still depends on that coding tool’s own GitHub or codebase connection, not on a Pylon MCP "create PR" tool. Can you turn support evidence into docs and analysis? Yes. Feed issue context into an AI tool to draft an internal note, a product brief, or an account summary, and combine Pylon data with other sources those tools can reach (for example Notion or Linear) when those connections are configured. How do you set up the Pylon MCP server? Step 1 Enable MCP Access Make sure each user or API token identity that connects has the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Access follows the same scoping as the Pylon dashboard. Step 2 Open the MCP Server settings in Pylon In Pylon, go to Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server. Copy your workspace’s regional MCP URL from Installation. Step 3 Connect your AI tool Add the URL in your AI tool’s MCP settings, or for ChatGPT install the Pylon app from Settings > Plugins. Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Transport is Streamable HTTP (stateless). US server: mcp.usepylon.com EU server: mcp.eu.usepylon.com See Pylon’s MCP docs for the full tool list. See the MCP setup guide for client steps. See how to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP. See how to connect Pylon to Claude with MCP. Frequently asked questions What is the Pylon MCP server? MCP is an open standard that lets AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor connect to external products. Pylon’s MCP server exposes your Pylon workspace (issues, accounts, contacts, and more) to those tools over OAuth 2.0 or an API token, so your team can query and act on support data from the AI clients they already use. Which AI tools can connect to Pylon via MCP? Pylon’s MCP server works with MCP clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and Cursor. For ChatGPT, the fastest path is Pylon’s native ChatGPT app; you can also add the regional MCP URL as a custom connector. Headless workers, scripts, and clients that support custom authorization headers can connect with an existing Pylon API token instead of OAuth. What actions can an AI tool take in Pylon through MCP? Connected AI tools can search and update issues, post internal notes, and send customer replies, which AI tools are instructed to show you for approval before sending. They can also manage accounts and contacts, draft and publish knowledge base articles, and work with macros, tags, and triggers. Tools for tasks, projects, account notes, and call recordings require Account Intelligence. Feature requests and some other tools require additional plan features. All actions stay within your Pylon permissions. Is the Pylon MCP server secure? Connections use OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions run as the signed-in user or the token’s identity, with that identity’s current role and permissions. No extra permissions are granted. The identity also needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. How do I set up the Pylon MCP server? Open Settings → AI Controls → MCP Server in Pylon, copy your regional URL (https://mcp.usepylon.com or https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com), and add it in your AI tool (or install the ChatGPT app). Sign in with OAuth, or send an existing API token in an Authorization: Bearer header if your client supports it. Is the Pylon MCP server on every plan? Yes. The pricing Features by tier table lists the Pylon MCP server on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise. Some individual MCP tools still require add-ons or plan features such as Account Intelligence. Other integrations Pylon also connects with the other AI tools your team already uses, plus Slack, email, CRMs, and more. pages.text: How to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP | Pylon The support metrics that matter in the age of AI Register now Resources Guides · November 6, 2026 How to connect Pylon to ChatGPT with MCP A practical how-to for support teams that want ChatGPT to work on Pylon issues and accounts without inventing a custom integration. Pylon Team · 5 min read You can connect ChatGPT to Pylon in two ways. The fastest is Pylon’s native ChatGPT app: install it from Settings > Plugins in ChatGPT (some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins) and sign in with your Pylon account. You can also add the Pylon MCP server to ChatGPT as a custom MCP server. Either way, ChatGPT authenticates with OAuth and uses tools that read or write the same data your user can already see in Pylon. This is a how-to for Pylon + ChatGPT . It is not a vendor roundup. For platform comparisons, see Customer support platforms that work with ChatGPT and MCP . Using Claude instead? See How to connect Claude to Pylon with MCP . What you need before you start From Pylon MCP docs : A Pylon workspace on a plan that includes the Pylon MCP server (listed on every plan in Features by tier ). A Pylon user with the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Permission for each tool operation you expect ChatGPT to run. MCP cannot return data the user cannot see, or write what the user cannot write in the Pylon UI. ChatGPT access that allows custom MCP servers or plugins. OpenAI documents workspace permissions and security restrictions, including Lockdown, for adding custom MCP servers ( Add custom MCP server ). Pylon side: get your MCP server URL In Pylon, open Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server . Copy your workspace’s regional MCP URL from Installation . Use that URL in your AI tool. Official server URLs published in docs: US: https://mcp.usepylon.com EU: https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com Auth is OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Transport is Streamable HTTP (stateless). Source: Pylon MCP . ChatGPT side: install the Pylon app In ChatGPT, open Settings > Plugins . Some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins. Search for Pylon and install Pylon’s ChatGPT app. When prompted, sign in with your Pylon account and authorize the connection. The ChatGPT app signs in with OAuth. The Pylon MCP server also accepts an API token for clients that support custom authorization headers. Your browser returns to ChatGPT, and Pylon’s tools are available in your conversations. If your ChatGPT workspace restricts apps, an admin may need to allow it first. Alternative: add Pylon as a custom MCP server Use this path if your workspace can’t install the Pylon app or you need a custom connection. OpenAI’s current public guide for ChatGPT on the web ( Add custom MCP server ; also Connect and test your plugin ): Go to ChatGPT Plugins. Select the plus button, then Add custom MCP server . Enter a name and optional description (for example, “Pylon”). Under Connection, enter your Server URL (the regional URL from Pylon Installation), or use Tunnel only if you are testing a private server with Secure MCP Tunnel. Configure authentication. For Pylon, choose OAuth (Pylon supports OAuth 2.0 or an API token). Review the risk warning and select that you understand and want to continue. Select Create as a plugin , then install the plugin before using it in a conversation. In a chat, type @ and select the installed plugin when you want ChatGPT to use Pylon tools. Supported transports in ChatGPT’s custom MCP flow include SSE and streaming HTTP. Write actions require confirmation by default. OpenAI treats tools without a readOnlyHint as write actions. Desktop note: ChatGPT desktop / Codex can also add MCP servers under Settings > MCP servers ( ChatGPT Learn: MCP ). Prefer the web plugin flow above for the public HTTPS Pylon server unless your team standardizes on desktop config. What ChatGPT can do after it connects Capabilities below come only from Pylon MCP . Summarized for buyers; the docs page is the full tool list. Issues (read and write): search and fetch issues and messages, create and update issues, snooze, send internal notes, send customer replies, manage followers and internal threads, link product tickets (Linear, Jira, GitHub, Asana, Shortcut). Important reply behavior: a customer reply goes out on the issue’s channel and cannot be unsent. Docs say AI tools are instructed to show the exact message and get approval before sending. Most AI tools also ask you to confirm each reply. Accounts and contacts: search and update accounts and contacts within your permissions. Knowledge base: search and read articles; draft, publish, and move content if you have the same edit and publish permissions as in Pylon. Plan-gated examples: Account notes and some account intelligence tools require Account Intelligence. Tasks and projects require Account Intelligence. Call recordings require Account Intelligence. Feature Requests tools require the Feature Requests plan feature. Audit log search requires Admin; full history is Enterprise, otherwise last 30 days. AI agent backtesting tools require AI Agents and Backtesting plus MCP Access and agent permissions. Rate limits apply per tool and organization. Throttling returns a JSON-RPC error with a retry delay. Safe first workflows Start with read-only work, then add writes you are willing to approve: “Find open issues for account Acme that mention SSO.” “Summarize the last 10 messages on issue 1842 for my internal note.” “Draft a reply, but do not send until I approve.” Only then: “Send the approved reply” or “Update the status after I confirm.” Do not paste API keys into ChatGPT. The ChatGPT connection signs in with OAuth as the authenticated user. FAQ Does Pylon support ChatGPT over MCP? Yes. Install Pylon’s native ChatGPT app from Settings > Plugins in ChatGPT (some older views, including very old iOS or Android apps, show Apps instead of Plugins), or add the Pylon MCP server as a custom MCP server. Both use OAuth and your normal Pylon permissions. Source: Pylon MCP docs . Where do I find my Pylon MCP URL? Open Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server in Pylon and copy the regional URL from Installation. Public base URLs are https://mcp.usepylon.com (US) and https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com (EU). Who can connect? Connecting needs the MCP Access permission, which the standard Member and Admin roles include. Each tool still checks the user’s normal Pylon permissions. Can ChatGPT send a customer reply from Pylon? Yes, through send_issue_reply , subject to your permissions. Docs require showing the exact message and getting approval before send because replies cannot be unsent. Is the Pylon MCP server on every plan? Yes. The pricing Features by tier table lists Pylon MCP server on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise. Some MCP tools still need add-ons or plan features such as Account Intelligence. How is this different from your MCP platforms blog? That post compares multiple vendors’ MCP or ChatGPT support. This post is only the setup path for Pylon and ChatGPT, with permissions and tool boundaries from Pylon docs and OpenAI’s custom MCP guide. Ready to try it on your workspace? Schedule a demo .
